summary.text: St. Abraham is the biblical patriarch called from his country to receive God’s promise of descendants, land and blessing for the nations.
summary.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

saints.context: The source’s received ecclesiastical narrative is identified as such. Uncertain dates, later traditions and unknown circumstances of death are retained as uncertain.

blocks.text: Genesis introduces St. Abraham under the earlier name Abram. God calls him to leave his country and kindred and go to a land that God will show him. The promise concerns a people and a blessing extending beyond his own household; he travels to Canaan in response.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: God confirms the covenant and changes his name to Abraham. His story includes receiving visitors at Mamre, interceding for a threatened city, and becoming the father of St. Isaac in old age. In Genesis 22 he takes Isaac to the place appointed for sacrifice; God stops the killing and provides a ram. Hebrews later presents this trial as an example of trust in God’s power to fulfill the promise.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: Genesis reports that St. Abraham dies at 175 years of age and is buried in the cave of Machpelah. This is the biblical lifespan, rather than an independently dated modern chronology. The narrative does not describe martyrdom.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: The OCA commemorates St. Abraham on October 9 and also among the Holy Forefathers before the Nativity. The latter observance is movable, occurring on the Sunday falling between December 11 and 17 in the church calendar.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: Romans 4 explains his faith in relation to God’s promise. Matthew places him at the beginning of Christ’s genealogy.

death.label: Death in old age in Genesis 25:7–10; no martyrdom described
